title: Review repair F: rejected/refused attempts are torn down honestly, spent() consults the local branch, a gate failure has a recovery path
description:
From the final re-review (findings at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-peterengelbrecht-Development-ticfac/1687f85b-9680-4c8b-ad98-ebe61eb3bfb3/scratchpad/review/reverify-findings.md, read-only on this host; JSON lines in new-defects.jsonl there). You own internal/reconcile; sibling repair E owns internal/exec/subprocess and doc/prompt wording. If you need an executor seam (e.g. a Cancel that is a no-op on a settled attempt), make the smallest change in internal/exec/subprocess/cancel.go and say so in RESULT-F.md so the sibling's merge is easy.

(1) dispatch.go:942 tearDown calls executor.Cancel before Dispose for a REJECTED attempt; Cancel writes cancel.json unconditionally (cancel.go:59-75) even when the attempt has already settled, and inspect's observe() reads cancel.json first (inspect.go:99-102). A resumed run re-adopting a rejected attempt that carried commits (not spent()) then inspects as cancelled and refuses with a sentence about an event that never happened. Revoke the credential without recording a stop when the attempt is already settled, and test the scenario: worker commits, reports BLOCKED, timer push landed, disposeRejected, operator resolves, epic run again, attempt adopted and handled on its real verdict. (2) dispatch.go:419 spent() judges 'left nothing' from origin's ref alone; a rejected attempt whose commits never reached origin (all pushes failed, integrate refusal at integrate.go:163-169) is declared spent once origin is back and a new attempt orphans the local branch that holds the only copy. On the same checkout consult the local branch (git rev-parse the attempt branch) before declaring spent; refuse with a message naming the branch when it carries work. (3) integrate.go:41,44,47,91 RefusedMerge, gate.go:105 RefusedGate, gate.go:124 RefusedStale and the four role-job refusals at rolejob.go:97-134 run no teardown: credential file stays live, worktree and local branch stay registered. Tear down on every refusal class the way disposeRejected does (revoke, dispose worktree, keep a branch that carries commits) — this closes the 7mj deferral, which is now decided: dispose role-job refusals too, the branch keeps the answer. (4) reconcile.go:638 the failed checkpoint's reason invites a resume, but a GATE failure cannot recover that way: the merge is already on the integration branch and gate evidence is keyed per (tick, attempt, check) create-if-absent (gate.go:145-150, 330-332), so the resume re-reads the recorded fail forever. Either key gate evidence by the commit it ran on when the previous record failed (so a fixed tree re-runs the gate), or make 'ticfac settle' accept a gate-failed attempt and say so in the reason. Test the operator-fixes-and-reruns path end to end. (5) nit, integrate.go:163: on a fresh-clone restart the corrective push may run in a clone lacking the object; make the refusal say the commit is not in this checkout rather than blaming origin. Use go test -short -timeout 45m for the reconcile package, foreground only.
